text: ECL1 crude-extract binding at aldA -59 to -6 increases with glycolaldehyde or 2-oxoglutarate. The factor identity and direct ligand binding remain unresolved; higher shifted bands do not establish subunit stoichiometry.

evidence.source_assertion: The deletion and binding experiment locates an unidentified crude-extract factor response in the aldA -59 to -6 region.
Glycolaldehyde and 2-oxoglutarate enhance crude-extract complexes; multimerization is a hypothesis rather than a defined purified regulator.

text: FucO domain swapping and the historical N-terminal deletion support assembly dependence. AldA has direct tetramer support; older dimer estimates are retained as conflicting measurements.

evidence.source_assertion: The FucO dimer exchanges N-terminal strands between subunits; this is a structural assembly interpretation.
The historical N-terminal deletion experiment reduces activity and alters oligomeric behavior; its numbering is not silently transferred to current P0A9S1.
Ultracentrifugation gives AldA about 211 kDa, consistent with a tetramer rather than an earlier dimer estimate.

text: Historical G97E lost tested activity whereas G17D retained it; D39G expanded cofactor use. The attempted 2005 glycolaldehyde complex lacked substrate density.

evidence.source_assertion: The tested G97E substitution abolishes measured activity and coenzyme interaction while G17D differs; this does not prove an EG-specific whole-cell effect.
D39G permits NADPH use in the tested mutant; the result is not a wild-type core NADPH side.
Attempts to obtain the glycolaldehyde ternary complex did not yield bound substrate density; the substrate-position model used propanediol.

text: 2007 endogenous untagged AldA co-purified with a pBSET taxadiene-synthase preparation. C285/E251 mechanism and coenzyme poses are models informed by lactaldehyde-related structures, not an observed productive EG-derived covalent intermediate.

evidence.source_assertion: The isolated AldA was an endogenous BL21(DE3) contaminant of a taxadiene-synthase preparation, not an engineered AldA target.
The structural discussion proposes catalytic residue and coenzyme roles. Crystal binding, partial occupancy and modeled chemistry do not establish physiological cofactor competence.

text: The 2023 reduction assays show cooperativity, K0.5 rather than Km, and preliminary ordered Bi-Bi behavior; H267Q/D360N retain activity. N151G/L259V 7QNF contains cryoprotectant EG and ADPR with unresolved nicotinamide, not a productive wild-type ternary intermediate.

evidence.source_assertion: The reduction kinetics show positive substrate cooperativity; the reported half-saturation quantity is K0.5, not an ordinary Michaelis constant.
The ordered Bi-Bi interpretation is preliminary because cooperative substrate behavior complicates the inference.
The mutant crystal contains EG used as cryoprotectant and unresolved nicotinamide; it does not demonstrate productive wild-type EG oxidation.
Mutant catalytic activity persists, limiting any claim that one proposed residue is uniquely responsible for the rate-limiting proton step.

text: The 2008 N-terminal His-tagged F180T BL21(DE3)pLysS preparation expands NADP use in propionaldehyde assays. Different NADH Ki values and reduced Mg response are mutant and assay dependent.

evidence.source_assertion: The engineered F180T comparison concerns altered coenzyme use. Its behavior cannot replace native AldA chemistry in the EG core.

text: The 2014 MG1655, deletion and 8myc ChIP study used anaerobic M9 glucose with or without nitrate. Specific aldA supplemental rows were not inspected; the gene-specific claim here remains the explicit native regulation.

evidence.source_assertion: Methods use MG1655 and derivatives, ArcA/Fnr-8myc constructs, 0.2% glucose, 0.1% ammonium chloride, nitrogen flushing and 20 mmol nitrate for nitrate respiration.
ChIP used tagged proteins and 300-1000 bp sonicated fragments, so the physical assay has regional resolution; its method does not itself prove an aldA-specific binding result.

text: MG1655-derived LMSE11/12 pTrc99a FucO I7L/L8V or L8M and AldA were tested with yeast extract; modeled diffusion and aeration effects remain engineering context.

evidence.source_assertion: The 2021 cultivation methods contain 2 g/L yeast extract. EG-supported engineering results are not automatically sole-organic-carbon or unmodified-reference growth.

text: MG1655 UV EG01 and DnaB-AID/evolved EG02 differ from the reference. Fig.4 identifies module III as the glycerate module; its performance resolves contradictory III/IV wording in Results. Defined M9 tests differ from mixed PET hydrolysate and EG-versus-LB RNA comparisons.

evidence.source_assertion: Figure 4 identifies modules I FucO/AldA, II GlcDEF, III Gcl/Hyi/GlxR/GlxK and IV GlcB. Module III supports growth in this test, while I alone does not; the body contains contradictory wording.
The primary methods separately specify defined M9 EG medium and the strains used, not ordinary unmodified MG1655 growth on all tested media.

text: Alternative engineered PedE/PQQ or Gox0313 catalysis and fucO/yqhD/glcDEF deletions are parallel pathways, not substitutions for this native core. The source inconsistently names MG1655 and MG1655(DE3); medium contains yeast extract.

evidence.source_assertion: The methods/table retain MG1655 and MG1655(DE3) names, engineered enzyme/deletion variants, 10 g/L EG and 2 g/L yeast extract. A defined native reference-growth claim is not warranted.

text: The reviewed AldA annotation also names p-hydroxy mercuribenzoate inhibition, and native annotation names glutamate induction. Neither phrase is assigned a forced chemical charge/stereoisomer in this record.

evidence.source_assertion: The exact issuing annotation names p-hydroxy mercuribenzoate among inhibitors. A neutral acid ontology label is not an adequate substitute for an unspecified mercuribenzoate charge or salt.
The native comment includes glutamate-associated induction; no exact ionic or stereochemical effector identity is supplied here.

text: The 1987 primary PDF was not acquired. A limited indexed excerpt supports earlier kinetic and tetramer context; 1983 identity and later mechanistic papers available only as abstracts remain explicitly bounded.

evidence.source_assertion: The inspected abstract reports coelution, common peptide maps and thermosensitivity supporting the glycolaldehyde/lactaldehyde dehydrogenase identity; no full-paper body access is claimed.
The inspected abstract proposes oxidative modification involving historical His277; this is not universal proof of the unique inactivation mechanism.
The abstract reports engineered FucO substitutions and expression changes; it does not establish ordinary wild-type EG growth.
The abstract reports engineered chromosomal EG assimilation and evolution; full-paper mechanisms were not inspected.

text: The native archaeal and yeast first-reaction annotations describe glycolaldehyde reduction toward EG; they do not establish the full oxidative EG route in those organisms. Their salt/metal/preparation context is not transferred to E. coli FucO.

evidence.source_assertion: The exact archaeal enzyme-reaction object has PHYSIOL-RIGHT-TO-LEFT direction and KCl-positive regulation. Internal pH/temperature direction qualifiers differ and are not used to reverse this pathway core.

The exact yeast object is a physiological reductase. It reports Cu/Ni/Zn and weaker Mn/Ca inhibition, under 10% Mg/Fe inhibition, and no major glycerol/betaME/EDTA/DTT effect; none is an E. coli FucO regulation.
The abstract describes a halophilic archaeal pentose route producing EG from glycolaldehyde, a different direction and pathway scope from two-step EG oxidation.
The abstract characterizes a yeast aldehyde reductase, with tagged recombinant preparation and reductive cofactor activity; it does not establish the full oxidative EG pathway in yeast.

text: Native comments retain adjacent physiological observations without expanding the two-event core.

evidence.source_assertion: The native FucO comment includes alternative alcohol and engineered reverse-beta-oxidation uses, colonization and codon effects. These are adjacent contexts, not additional core EG events.
The native AldA comment includes other carbon/folate contexts and prpC synthetic lethality. Genetic interaction is not evidence that PrpC catalyzes AldA chemistry.

text: Native gene-specific annotations remain distinct from paper-wide abstracts and neighboring promoter mechanisms.

evidence.source_assertion: The abstract describes MarA/SoxS/Rob transcriptional activation across a regulon. It does not by itself establish that aldA was directly bound; the native gene-specific expression assertions allow indirectness.
The abstract studies selected fucPIK regulatory suppression involving IS5 and CRP. This mechanism is not automatically a purified fucAO promoter-binding result.
The native source separately records a mapped fucO transcription unit; it is not collapsed into the fucAO TU00135 regulatory context.

text: The 2005 source reports earlier Cu(II)/Cd(II) FucO inhibition and cites PMID4306747. Retained evidence for the older paper is abstract/landing material; its full experimental body was not inspected. Figure 4 tests Zn/Fe, so no Cu/Cd dose, EG oxidation effect, binding mechanism or new causal edge is asserted.

evidence.source_assertion: The 2005 discussion reports earlier FucO inhibition by Cu(II) and Cd(II), citing reference 40. This is prior-work context; the adjacent Figure 4 experiment addresses Zn/Fe.
Reference 40 links the earlier oxidoreductase study to PMID4306747. This citation identifies the prior report; it does not supply a freshly inspected older experimental body.

text: The 0.53 Fe atom/subunit WT solution comparator occurs in a site-directed-mutant comparison. Methods assign those WT/mutant preparations to pCM2 GST/factor-Xa cleavage in BL21(DE3). This is an explicit Methods/Results attribution, distinct from pCM1 His6 crystal-site evidence, and is not universal iron occupancy.

evidence.source_assertion: Methods state that WT and mutant FucO preparations for site-directed-mutagenesis studies used pGEX3X/pCM2 in BL21(DE3), with GST removed by factor Xa to avoid the His6 tag.

Results compare D196L, H200A and H200F metal contents with WT examined in parallel, reporting 0.53 Fe atom/subunit for WT. Read with the preparation Methods, this supports the cleaved-WT comparator attribution, not His6 crystal occupancy.
